compounds.name: Nitrile (Buna-N)
compounds.note: The default, cheapest and most available. Excellent in mineral oil, fuel and grease.
compounds.watch: Poor ozone and UV resistance: cracks even in storage. Not for phosphate esters, ketones or hot water.

compounds.name: Hydrogenated nitrile
compounds.note: Nitrile with the ozone weakness engineered out and a useful temperature gain. Very good abrasion resistance.
compounds.watch: Considerably more expensive than NBR. Still not for phosphate esters.

compounds.name: Fluoroelastomer (Viton)
compounds.note: The aerospace and high-temperature workhorse. Wide chemical range, low gas permeability, excellent compression set hot.
compounds.watch: Check the COLD end: standard grades stiffen around −20 °C. Not for steam, hot water, ketones, amines or phosphate esters. Low-temperature grades (GLT) exist.

compounds.name: Perfluoroelastomer (Kalrez)
compounds.note: Near-universal chemical resistance with the highest temperature capability of any elastomer.
compounds.watch: Extraordinarily expensive: often priced per seal. Poor low-temperature flexibility. Specify only where nothing else works.

compounds.name: Ethylene propylene diene
compounds.note: The correct choice for phosphate ester hydraulic fluid (Skydrol), brake fluid, hot water and steam. Excellent weathering.
compounds.watch: Completely unsuitable for mineral oils, fuels and greases: it swells and disintegrates. The single most common misapplication in the seal world.

compounds.name: Silicone
compounds.note: Widest temperature range of the common elastomers, physiologically inert, excellent compression set when hot.
compounds.watch: Poor tear, abrasion and tensile strength. STATIC DUTY ONLY. Permeable to gases. Silicone contamination destroys adhesive bonds nearby.

compounds.name: Fluorosilicone
compounds.note: Silicone's cold capability with fuel resistance: a classic aerospace fuel-system seal for cold environments.
compounds.watch: Weak mechanically like silicone; static duty. Expensive.

compounds.name: Neoprene (chloroprene)
compounds.note: Good all-rounder with genuine weather and ozone resistance. Common in refrigerants and marine service.
compounds.watch: Middling at everything: usually beaten by NBR on oil or EPDM on water. Chosen mainly for refrigerant compatibility.

compounds.name: Polyurethane
compounds.note: Outstanding extrusion and abrasion resistance: the high-pressure hydraulic choice where an elastomer would extrude.
compounds.watch: Hydrolyses in hot or humid conditions (polyester grades especially). Narrow temperature range.

compounds.name: Aflas (TFE/propylene)
compounds.note: Resists steam, amines and strong bases where FKM fails. Oilfield and chemical process favourite.
compounds.watch: Very poor low-temperature flexibility. Limited availability and long lead times.

compounds.name: Butyl
compounds.note: Exceptionally low gas permeability: the vacuum and gas-retention choice.
compounds.watch: Not for hydrocarbons. Poor rebound (that's why it damps well).

compounds.name: PTFE-encapsulated (FEP/PFA over core)
compounds.note: A silicone or FKM core inside a seamless fluoropolymer jacket: near-universal chemical resistance with elastomeric recovery.
compounds.watch: Cannot be stretched much on assembly: needs a split or dismountable groove. Higher squeeze forces; check the gland can generate them. STATIC duty.
